description: Yinchen Yi and Yutong Li publish a reusable Los Angeles case study linking earthquake damage to substations, restoration-crew travel and census-tract service disparities. The July 2026 archive contains a Python 3.12 workflow, required and derived inputs, retained simulation outputs and manuscript figures. Six stages assemble topology, ground shaking, travel times, analysis and figures. The repository explicitly uses graph-based service recovery, not electrical power flow. Historical ShakeMap scenarios and a California Geological Survey hazard scenario supply shaking inputs; this is a scenario study, not an observed citywide recovery record. Original code is free under MIT, while third-party data retain their own terms. Git LFS is required for large inputs. Related catalogue resources include FEMA's National Risk Index and the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index. The authors report lightweight release checks but no full Monte Carlo or genetic-algorithm rerun during release validation; this review executed neither.
